title: The wise men part 2
scripture_text: ‘’After Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea, during the time of King Herod, Magi from the east came to Jerusalem and asked, “Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw his star when it rose and have come to worship him.” When King Herod heard this he was disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him. When he had called together all the people’s chief priests and teachers of the law, he asked them where the Messiah was to be born. “In Bethlehem in Judea,” they replied, “for this is what the prophet has written: “But you, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for out of you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.’’ Then Herod called the Magi secretly and found out from them the exact time the star had appeared. He sent them to Bethlehem and said, “Go and search carefully for the child. As soon as you find him, report to me, so that I too may go and worship him.” After they had heard the king, they went on their way, and the star they had seen when it rose, went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the child was. When they saw the star, they were overjoyed. On coming to the house, they saw the child with his mother Mary, and they bowed down and worshipped him. Then they opened their treasures and presented him with gifts of gold, frankincense and myrrh. And having been warned in a dream not to go back to Herod, they returned to their country by another route.’’
devotional:
There are four things that Herod did in his attempt to eradicate the threat he was feeling.

1. He was motivated by his emotions.

Herod allowed his emotions to control his thinking and determine his actions. He was paranoid and irrational. As we have seen he was in acute mental distress. There is in verse 4 something that we don’t pick up in our English translations. When we are told that he asked the teachers of the law, where the Messiah was to be born, it would be better understood that he kept on asking and asking and asking. There was a sense of panic and paranoia. Paranoia is very debilitating, and will always keep a person from truly worshipping Jesus, because it produces within a person a fear that ensures that they become the centre of their universe. There will always be a need to protect whatever is under threat, in this case it was Herod's throne.

b. He made plans in secret.

Look at verse 7. ‘Herod called for a private meeting.’ There was a duplicity, a hidden agenda about Herod, but even worse, he wanted to involved others in his duplicity. Herod must have been very convincing because God had to warn the wise men of Herod's evil plan. There is always something intrinsically deceitful in the act of trying to keep control, or when we strive to hold onto a position of power or prestige.

c. He needed to lie in order to secure his objective.

‘When you find him come back and tell me so I can worship him.’ This was the use of spiritual language to express a bare face lie. He was hiding behind a claim that he wanted to worship Jesus.

d. He lashed out at others.]

Read verses Matthew 2:16-18. He was furious and innocent baby boys lost their lives. Sometimes the fear of not being in control can cause us to lash out at others causing them to suffer. We may not be cruel and barbaric like Herod, but sometimes when we are feeling threatened and out of control of our circumstances, we can lash out at others. When our ‘thrones’ are threatened we can go into fight mode to protect our lordship over our own lives.
prayer: Father help me to continually hand control of my life over to Jesus.
